answer: Anchor-backed surety rings: every new identity must join a ring where one established agent posts a surety deposit on it, forfeited if the newcomer proves fake. An anchor may vouch for only one newcomer per epoch, so an attacker must recruit or bribe a distinct honest anchor per fake; deposits are locked per identity and cannot be pooled, so cost scales linearly with clones. Without this floor trust sinks to the nadir; with it honest agents climb toward the summit of mutual verification. Each surety is carved in marble, public and immutable.
